sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or complete the table).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Selling goods to foreign countries is ______. (b) Buying goods from foreign countries is ______.
questions.answer:
(a) exports
(b) imports

questions.q: Match: (a) Multinational corporations like Ford and Coca-Cola — ? (b) Does not have democracy — ? [China / USA]
questions.answer:
(a) USA (they emerged from the USA).
(b) China.

questions.q: State True or False: (a) Buying from foreign countries is exports. (b) Trade gives a variety of goods.
questions.answer:
(a) False — it is imports.
(b) True.

questions.q: Match: (a) Selling to foreign citizens — ? (b) International trade leads to — ? [specialisation / exports]
questions.answer:
(a) Exports.
(b) Specialisation.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Through trade people get a lot of ______ and choice. (b) Exports and imports of goods and services are ______ trade.
questions.answer:
(a) variety
(b) international

questions.q: Give one word: (a) The international currency of the USA. (b) The group of oil-exporting countries from which India imports petroleum.
questions.answer:
(a) US dollar ($).
(b) OPEC.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name India's main imports.
questions.answer: Petroleum and lubricants (from OPEC countries such as Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia), non-ferrous metals, capital goods such as machinery and transport equipment, and fertilisers.

questions.q: Distinguish between imports and exports.
questions.answer:
Exports: selling domestic goods and services to citizens of foreign countries, which earns foreign exchange.
Imports: buying goods and services from foreign countries, which uses foreign exchange.

questions.q: 'Trading activities are an integral part of the economy.' Explain.
questions.answer: Goods reach buyers wherever they live only through trade. Trains, trucks, ships and aeroplanes carry goods within and between countries, so distribution and consumption depend on trade.

questions.q: How does trade encourage new goods and services?
questions.answer: Through trade, sellers meet buyers and learn their choices and preferences. So they design and produce new goods and services to suit them, and foreign goods reach new markets.

questions.q: What is globalisation?
questions.answer: Globalisation is the process of countries coming closer together through trade, transport and communication (TV, internet, mobile phones), so that people consume foreign goods, work abroad and exchange ideas freely.

questions.q: Has online shopping become popular? Why?
questions.answer: Yes. With the internet, people can order goods, even from Germany or Japan, from home, compare prices, get a wide variety, and have the goods delivered to their door.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Compare the USA and China in manufacturing.
questions.answer:
USA manufacturing output was more than that of China, India and Brazil together. Its major industries are petroleum, steel, automobiles, and construction and farm machinery.
China's manufacturing grew very fast after its 1980s reforms and is said to have overtaken the USA in 2010. Its large-scale output made it the world's leading exporter (10% of world exports).

or.q: Why does China attract more foreign money than India?
or.answer:
China has a better economic environment for investors: fast growth after reforms, large-scale industry, strict implementation of plans and policies, and better population control.
So foreign investors put more money into its industries and services than into India's.

questions.q: Compare India with China in any three ways.
questions.answer:
(1) Political system: India is a democracy; China has one-party rule.
(2) Growth: both were similar till the 1980s, but China's national and per-capita income now grow faster.
(3) Trade: China had 10% of world exports in 2010 against India's 1.4%.
(4) Poverty: China's fell to 2.5% in 2005 against India's 27.5%. Both follow five-year plans.

questions.q: What are the advantages of international trade?
questions.answer:
(1) A variety of goods: we get foreign goods such as Coca-Cola, and others buy Indian pickles.
(2) New goods are produced to suit buyers' choices.
(3) People meet and learn other cultures.
(4) Specialisation: each country produces what it makes best and cheapest — India's spices and handicrafts — so prices fall.

questions.q: Name India's major exports and the countries they reach.
questions.answer:
Exports: engineering goods, handicrafts, chemicals, ready-made garments, cotton yarn, iron ore, leather, fish, rice, fruit and vegetables.
Destinations: France, Germany, the UK, the USA, Iran, the UAE, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and countries in Africa and Latin America.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write a short note on the economy of the USA.
questions.answer:
(1) One of the most developed economies and a large democracy, like India.
(2) The private sector dominates and the government interferes little. It has 30 million small businesses and 139 of the world's 500 largest companies, and about 40% of the world's richest people live there.
(3) Multinationals such as Ford, GE, Coca-Cola and Walmart come from the USA.
(4) Agriculture is advanced; it exports wheat, corn and fruit. Its manufacturing (petroleum, steel, automobiles, machinery) is huge.
(5) Education and health are of high quality, and the dollar is an international currency.
(6) Yet it has poverty (16% lacked good food in 2008) and unemployment (9.9% in 2010).

or.q: Write a short note on the economy of China.
or.answer:
(1) The second-largest economy in the world. It was like India until the 1980s and grew fast after economic reforms.
(2) No democracy: one party rules, but the private sector was gradually allowed.
(3) It follows five-year plans (first 1953–57, twelfth 2011–15).
(4) It had 10% of world exports in 2010 against India's 1.4%, and attracts more foreign money.
(5) Better population control; poverty fell from 51% (1981) to 2.5% (2005).

questions.q: Explain the importance of foreign trade for India.
questions.answer:
(1) It gives Indians a variety of goods — petroleum, machinery, fertilisers and consumer goods not made enough at home.
(2) It earns foreign exchange through exports of engineering goods, garments, handicrafts, spices and IT services.
(3) Specialisation: India exports goods it produces cheaply (spices, cotton, handicrafts) and imports others, so resources are used efficiently.
(4) It encourages new goods, technology and contact with other cultures.
(5) It links India to the global economy (globalisation) and creates jobs in export industries.

questions.q: Describe five types of economic relationship India has with other countries.
questions.answer:
(1) Exports — selling goods and services abroad, e.g. garments and IT.
(2) Imports — buying goods from abroad, e.g. petroleum and machinery.
(3) Sending and receiving gifts.
(4) Sending and receiving money, e.g. remittances by Indians working abroad.
(5) Visits by tourists, business people and government delegations.
A country with such relations is an open economy.

or.q: Name six export and four import items of India.
or.answer:
Exports: engineering goods, handicrafts, chemicals, ready-made garments, cotton yarn, leather (also iron ore, fish, rice).
Imports: petroleum and lubricants, non-ferrous metals, capital goods (machinery, transport equipment), fertilisers.

questions.q: Describe how trading activities are an integral part of the economy.
questions.answer:
Trade carries goods from where they are produced to whoever wants to buy them, by trains and trucks within the country and by ships and aeroplanes abroad.
Without trade, production would have no market and consumers would lack variety.
Trade gives choice, encourages new goods, brings people and cultures together, and leads to specialisation and lower costs.
Shops, markets, transport and communication — the whole service sector — grow around trade.
